overall: Atlanta is tracking a notably suppressed warming pattern for mid-June: the running max has been locked at 73.4°F since at least 7:00 AM, and by 11:35 ET the current temperature of 69.8°F has actually fallen below that peak, with zero warming velocity. Calm winds and a dewpoint of 62.6°F suggest lingering cloud cover or moisture is blunting solar heating well into the late morning hours, which is atypical for this time of year and this time of day.
forecast_obs_notes: Models show meaningful spread — HRRR at 75.5°F is the most conservative and aligns best with the stalled observed trend, while NBM at 79.2°F implies ~6°F of warming still to come, which looks increasingly difficult to achieve with velocity at 0.0°F/hr approaching solar noon. The even ensemble model (74–75°F) corroborates the bearish HRRR signal; the odd model's 81–82°F top would require an aggressive afternoon recovery inconsistent with current conditions.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max frozen at 73.4°F and temperatures actually retreating to 69.8°F by mid-morning with zero upward velocity, the path to the 79–82°F model range is very unlikely barring a sudden cloud break and rapid destabilization. The most probable outcome is a modest afternoon rebound that pushes the daily high to the mid-70s, with HRRR's 75.5°F serving as the best anchor; confidence is moderate-to-good on a finish in the 74–76°F range, with meaningful downside risk if cloud cover persists through the afternoon peak window.
